function.name: requests_get
function.description: Sends a GET request to the specified URL to retrieve weather data from the Open-Meteo API. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: URL of the Open-Meteo API endpoint.

headers.description: Headers to include in the request. Each key-value pair represents a header field and its value.

Content-Type.description: The MIME type of the body of the request (used with POST and PUT requests).

Accept.description: Media type(s) that is/are acceptable for the response.

timeout.description: Maximum time in seconds to wait for the server to send data before giving up. This is a float type value.

params.description: Query parameters for the GET request.

latitude.description: Latitude of the location, positive for N and negative for S. This is a float type value.

longitude.description: Longitude of the location, positive for E and negative for W. This is a float type value.

elevation.description: Elevation in meters above sea level for the location. The default value represents no elevation downscaling.

auth.description: Authentication tuple for HTTP authentication, in the format (username, password).

cert.description: Path to the SSL client certificate file (.pem). A null value means no client certificate is used.

cookies.description: Dictionary of cookies to send with the request. Each key represents a cookie name.

proxies.description: Dictionary mapping protocol names to the URL of the proxy. Each key-value pair represents a protocol and its proxy URL.

stream.description: If True, the response should be streamed; otherwise, it should be downloaded immediately.

verify.description: Whether to verify the server's TLS certificate.

Below is a quick “next‑up” snapshot of the most prominent festivals happening in the United States after **May 19 2026**.  
I’ve chosen events that are widely attended, have a long‑standing reputation, and cover a range of interests (music, food, comics, film, etc.).  If you’re looking for something more niche (e.g., a local street fair, a craft‑beer festival, or a regional cultural celebration), let me know and I can dig deeper.

| # | Festival | Dates (2026) | Location | What to Expect | Admission | Website |
|---|----------|--------------|----------|----------------|-----------|---------|
| 1 | **Summerfest** | **July 12 – 18** | Milwaukee, WI | The world’s largest music festival – 8 days, 70+ stages, 1,000+ acts spanning rock, pop, hip‑hop, country, EDM, and more.  Food trucks, craft beer, kids’ zone, and a massive “Summerfest Village.” | $25–$35 (early‑bird) to $45–$55 (late‑day) | <https://www.summerfest.com> |
| 2 | **Taste of Chicago** | **July 15 – 17** | Chicago, IL | The world’s largest food festival – 200+ restaurants, 100+ food trucks, live music, cooking demos, and a kids’ zone.  3‑day event with a “Taste of Chicago” parade. | Free (though some food stalls charge) | <https://www.tasteofchicago.com> |
| 3 | **Comic‑Con International** | **July 20 – 23** | San Diego, CA | The biggest pop‑culture convention in the world – comics, movies, TV, anime, gaming, cosplay, panels, and exclusive premieres.  4‑day event with a massive cosplay parade. | $49–$59 (early‑bird) to $69–$79 (late‑day) | <https://www.comic-con.org> |
| 4 | **Burning Man** | **Aug 28 – Sep 5** | Black Rock Desert, NV | The iconic art‑and‑self‑expression festival – 9 days of art installations, music, performance, and a “Burning Man” ceremony.  Participants bring their own supplies; it’s a “leave‑no‑trace” event. | $225–$275 (early‑bird) to $275–$325 (late‑day) | <https://burningman.org> |
| 5 | **Oktoberfest** | **Sept 1 – 10** | New York City, NY | NYC’s largest Oktoberfest – German beer, bratwurst, pretzels, live music, and a carnival atmosphere.  10‑day event with a parade. | Free (food & drinks sold on site) | <https://www.nyckoberfest.com> |
| 6 | **New York Comic Con** | **Oct 6 – 9** | New York City, NY | The second‑largest comic‑con in the U.S. – panels, celebrity guests, exclusive merch, and a huge cosplay parade. | $49–$59 (early‑bird) to $69–$79 (late‑day) | <https://nycc.com> |
| 7 | **Sundance Film Festival** | **Jan 20 – 30** | Park City, UT | The premier independent film festival – world premieres, retrospectives, panels, and a “Sundance Film Festival” awards ceremony. | $25–$35 (early‑bird) to $45–$55 (late‑day) | <https://www.sundance.org> |

---

### Why Summerfest is the “next” big thing

- **Timing**: It starts just 3 weeks after May 19, so it’s the first major festival you’ll see on the calendar.
- **Scale**: With 70+ stages and 1,000+ acts, it’s a one‑stop destination for almost every music taste.
- **Family‑friendly**: Kids’ zones, interactive art installations, and a “Summerfest Village” make it great for all ages.
- **Accessibility**: Milwaukee is a major city with plenty of hotels, public transit, and a vibrant downtown.

If you’re planning to attend, consider booking lodging early (the city fills up fast) and buying tickets in advance to lock in the lower early‑bird prices.

---

### Quick Tips for Planning

| Tip | Detail |
|-----|--------|
| **Book Lodging Early** | Hotels in the city center or near the festival grounds fill up quickly. |
| **Check Transportation** | Milwaukee has a light rail system (METRO) that runs to the festival grounds. |
| **Pack Smart** | Bring a reusable water bottle, a small backpack, and a rain poncho (weather can be unpredictable). |
| **Explore the Village** | The “Summerfest Village” offers food, art, and interactive experiences beyond the stages. |
| **Stay Safe** | Keep an eye on your belongings, stay hydrated, and follow the festival’s safety guidelines. |

---

### Want More Options?

If you’re interested in a different type of festival—say, a food‑only event, a craft‑beer gathering, a regional cultural celebration, or a niche music genre—just let me know the kind of experience you’re after, and I’ll pull up a tailored list.
